nom: Naturium Vitamin C Super Serum Plus

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily or combination-oily (T-zone) skin report the niacinamide helps reduce oil production without making them shinier, and one notes fewer enlarged pores without added oiliness.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin describe the serum as hydrating, non-drying, and lightweight, though one with normal-to-dry skin saw no visible benefit and developed milia.
segments.combination: A combination/oily (T-zone) reviewer reports a noticeable improvement in complexion and even skin tone.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers are split: several report no irritation and good tolerance even with retinol and salicylic acid in the formula, while others describe redness, itching, raised bumps, reopened wounds, or breakouts, sometimes despite a clean patch test.
segments.normal: One reviewer describes her skin as normal-to-dry and reports no clear improvement and new milia.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their 40s, 50s, and 70s report visible improvement in fine lines, firmness, and overall skin appearance, with no negative effects mentioned in this age group.

concerns.aging: Multiple reviewers report reduced fine lines, improved firmness, and brighter, more even-toned skin, including a 78-year-old and a 42-year-old noting visible change within 48 hours; no dissent specific to aging is reported.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers describe the serum as hydrating, plumping, and non-drying even for dry skin; one reviewer felt it was 'not terribly moisturizing' beyond a bare minimum.
concerns.redness: Some reviewers with sensitive skin experienced new redness, splotchy or raised bumps, and irritation after use, while others with sensitive skin report zero redness or reaction; effects appear inconsistent.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer with a previously compromised moisture barrier reports the serum, combined with other changes, helped as part of recovery; another reports irritation and painful under-skin pimples suggesting barrier stress.
concerns.spots: Several reviewers report fading dark spots, hyperpigmentation, and melasma improvement over weeks to months; one reviewer with sensitive/dry skin says hyperpigmentation did not improve for her.
concerns.blemishes: Many reviewers, including acne-prone ones, report clearer skin, fewer breakouts, and improved acne scars; several others report the opposite — new cystic pimples, congested pores, blackheads, or worsened acne, particularly among sensitive-skin users combining actives.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily/combination skin report the niacinamide content helps control oil production and reduces shine without over-drying; no negative reports on oiliness are present.

aspects.libelle: Multiple actives in one product saves routine steps

extraits.texte: I was looking for a new Vit C serum that was more affordable but also to treat a new facial scar I acquired from stitches. I'd fallen out of my skin care habits and the new injury was pushing me to get back to it. I was excited to try this having heard good things about it and the brand. I'd spent probably too much time researching. I had Dr OK to move to skincare treatment, so I started using it. Unfortunately, my research led me astray and this serum wasn't it. Not only did it reopen the previously closed wound, it irritated uninjured skin. While I do have sensitive skin, this seemed excessive. I tried for a two days, but ultimately gave up. Between wound reopening and painful under the skin pimples, this wasn't for me.

I thought I could save a few steps in my routine by using this over my individual ordinary serums and Vit C powder. My skin broke out terribly (pimples but congested pores and blackheads) and got very irritated. I think there are just too many ingredients and the vit C is not stable. After a week of use, my skin is also visibly duller after I replaced my vit C powder with this.

extraits.titre: Mixed feelings/-: Just not for me…
extraits.texte: I want to start off by saying that I have not had very good luck with retinol products in the past, and I was really hoping this product would be different. When I started using this, I stopped taking my birth control which I had been on for 8 years to control my acne. I had always struggled with blackheads and whiteheads and the occasional pimple but never anything crazy. I started using this product and a month in I was experiencing lots of pimples, but no whiteheads or blackheads like I was expecting since I stopped the pill. I assumed it was just the purge that everyone talks about when using retinol. I am halfway through my second bottle, three months into using this product, and my acne has only gotten worse. I have never experienced acne like this in my entire life. I have large pimples all over my forehead and painful pimples all over my cheeks and chin. Although, the places I don't have any acne are actually very smooth, supple, and the fine lines and hyperpigmentation are gone. I really wish this product worked for me, I was hoping it would be the cure-all I was looking for, but I am starting to think I may just have more sensitive skin because my body is readjusting. This product is so nice and left my skin feeling so soft, except for the acne breakouts. I would recommend it if you don't have issues with retinol and/or sensitive skin.

extraits.titre: A super-charged serum with many benefits!!
extraits.texte: At first, I was scared to use this product due to the presence of many actives within its formula. And considering my sensitive, dry skin, I was even more worried about the effects of this serum. But this serum... wow!! The Niacinamide helped me with my skin sensitivity and sebum production. The BHA helped me with my fine lines, wrinkles, and acne. The HA helped me with hydration. And the Vitamin C and Retinol helped me with aging effects. The only thing that I noticed that the serum did not improve on my skin was the effects of hyperpigmentation. I still am on the hunt of the perfect product to help me with hyperpigmentation.

This Serum is so good, I use it am and pm. It can be layered under Sunscreen and makeup. If you have combination/oily skin, the Niacinamide is helpful in reducing oil production. It does not irritate the skin.

I've been putting off using vitamin c for a while because of the issues with oxidation and also just adding another step to my routine sounded honestly annoying. Really love that this incorporates many powerhouse elements to my routine in one step. Easy to add to my skin care - I'm several weeks in, MINOR purging/adjustment phase but that could just be from the products I removed from my routine as well. I am seeing BRIGHTENING honey. My skin is PLUMP mama. My face had a lovely TONE babes. This doesn't pill and layers nicely with other products. Gonna use this forever truly. And I love the way it smells! It's not scented it just smells like...nice medicine for my skin. My skin was freaking out a couple months ago - cystic acne everywhere, messed up moisture barrier, clustering of acne, 3 pimple patches a NIGHT- and now with fewer actives in my routine, added moisture, more ceramides and THIS SERUM, I'm finally starting the work on fixing some hyperpigmentation and adding to a nice healthy tone for my skin.

I've always wondered why other companies sell serums with a singular active ingredient (hint: it's to make more money) but I finally found The One with everything I need! I was hesitant about it having salicylic acid and retinol with my dry, sensitive skin but I've had no irritation or flaking, even using it daily! The formula is super light and leaves zero residue. Wonderful.
